cues.en: When people look at it, it looks crazy. That's a very natural thing. Sometimes when we look at it, it looks crazy. It is the result of reasoned engineering thought. But it still looks crazy. From the top of the atmosphere down to the surface, it takes us seven minutes. It takes 14 minutes or so for the signal from the spacecraft.
cues.zh: 人们看到它时，会觉得这很疯狂。这很自然。有时我们看着它，也觉得疯狂。它是理性工程思考的结果。但它看起来仍然疯狂。从大气层顶部到地表，我们需要七分钟。而来自航天器的信号大约需要14分钟。

cues.en: To make it to Earth, that's how far Mars is away from us. So, when we first get word that we've touched the top of the atmosphere, the vehicle has been alive and we're dead on the surface for at least seven minutes. Entry-descent landing, also known as EDL, is referred to as a seven minutes of terror because we've got literally seven minutes to get from the top of the atmosphere to the surface of Mars.
cues.zh: 要到达地球，这就是火星离我们的距离。所以，当我们第一次得知已经触到大气层顶部时，飞行器要么还活着，要么已经在表面坠毁，而这一切已经发生了至少七分钟。进入、下降与着陆，也叫 EDL，被称为“恐怖七分钟”，因为我们真的只有七分钟时间，从大气层顶部到火星表面。

cues.en: going from 13,000 miles an hour to zero in perfect sequence, perfect choreography, perfect timing, and the computer has to do it all by itself with no help from the ground. If any one thing doesn't work just right, it's game over. We slam into the atmosphere and develop so much aerodynamic drag. Our heat shield, it heats up and it glows like the surface of the sun. 1600 degrees.
cues.zh: 从每小时13,000英里降到零，整个过程必须顺序完美、编排完美、时机完美，而计算机必须完全靠自己完成，不能靠地面帮助。只要有任何一件事不对，就完蛋了。我们猛冲进大气层，产生巨大的气动阻力。我们的隔热罩会升温，亮得像太阳表面。1600度。

cues.en: During entry, the vehicle is not only slowing down violently through the atmosphere, but also we are guiding it like an airplane to be able to land in a very narrow constraint space. This is one of the biggest challenges that we are facing and one that we have never attempted on Mars. Mars is actually really hard to slow down because it has just enough atmosphere that you have to deal with it. Otherwise, it will destroy your spacecraft.
cues.zh: 进入过程中，飞行器不仅在大气层中剧烈减速，我们还要像驾驶飞机一样引导它，使它能够落在非常狭窄的约束空间内。这是我们面临的最大挑战之一，也是我们在火星上从未尝试过的。火星实际上很难减速，因为它的大气层刚好浓到你必须应对它；否则，它会摧毁你的航天器。

cues.en: On the other hand, it doesn't have enough atmosphere to finish the job. We're still going about 1,000 miles an hour. So at that point, we use a parachute. The parachute is the largest and strongest supersonic parachute that we've ever built to date. It has to be able to withstand 65,000 pounds of force, even though the parachute itself only weighs about 100 pounds. When it opens up that fast, it's a neck-snapping 9G's.
cues.zh: 另一方面，它没有足够的大气层来完成这个任务。我们仍然以大约每小时1000英里的速度飞行。所以到那个阶段，我们就用降落伞。这个降落伞是我们迄今为止建造的最大、最强的超音速降落伞。它必须能承受65000磅的力，尽管降落伞本身只有大约100磅重。当它那么快地打开时，会产生像扭断脖子一样的9G过载。

cues.en: At that point, we have to get that heat chilled off. It's like a big lens cap blocking our view of the ground to the radar. The radar has to take just the right altitude and velocity measurements at just the right time, or the rest of the landing sequence won't work. This big, huge parachute that we've got, it will only slow us down to about 200 miles an hour. And that's not slow enough to land. So we have no choice, but we've got to cut it off and come down in rockets.
cues.zh: 到那时，我们必须把那层热量散去。它就像一个大镜头盖，挡住了雷达对地面的视线。雷达必须在恰到好处的时机取得恰到好处的高度和速度测量，否则剩下的着陆序列就无法进行。我们拥有的这个巨大的降落伞，只会把我们减速到大约每小时200英里。而这还不足以慢到可以着陆。所以我们别无选择，只能把它切掉，靠火箭降落下来。

cues.en: Once we turn those rocket motors on, if we don't do something, we're just going to smack right back into the parachute. So the first thing we do is make this really radical divert. We fly off to the side, diverting away from the parachute, killing our horizontal velocity and our vertical velocity, getting it over, moving straight up and down so it can look at the surface with its radar and see where we're going to land. And we head straight down to the bottom of a crater, right beside.
cues.zh: 一旦我们点燃那些火箭发动机，如果不做点什么，我们就会直接撞回降落伞上。所以我们做的第一件事就是做一个非常激进的转向。我们飞到一边，偏离降落伞，抵消水平速度和垂直速度，把它转过来，垂直上下移动，这样它就能用雷达观察表面，看看我们要在哪里着陆。然后我们直接朝一个陨石坑底部降落，就在旁边。

cues.en: a 6-kilometer high mount. We can't get those rocket engines too close to the ground because if we were to descend propulsively with our engines all the way to the ground, we would essentially create this massive dust cloud. That dust cloud could then go and land on the rover, it could damage mechanisms, and it could damage instruments. So the way we solved that problem is by using the sky crane over there. 20 meters above the surface, you have to lower the rover below us on a tether that's 21 feet long, and then gently deposit it.
cues.zh: 一座6公里高的山。我们不能让火箭发动机离地面太近，因为如果全程依靠发动机动力下降一直到地面，基本上会掀起巨大的尘暴。这些沙尘会落到火星车上，可能损坏机械结构和仪器设备。因此我们解决这个问题的办法，就是使用那边的“天空起重机”。在距离地表20米的高空，需要用一根21英尺长的缆绳把火星车悬吊降下，然后轻轻地放置

cues.en: on its wings, on the surface. As the rover touches down and is now on the ground, to the same stage, it's an air pollution force with a rover. We must cut the bridle immediately and fly to the same stage to a safe distance from the rover.
cues.zh: 平稳着陆在地表上。当火星车触地并停稳后，为避免与下降级产生拉扯，我们必须立刻切断系缆，并将下降级飞离到距离火星车足够安全的地方。
